title: Prove exact Boolean directed-cycle tariff 108 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration, produced by Nick Petalas. This settles one independently directed-price family left open in lee-phys's [PR5304](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5304), for the Boolean demand `(110,101,011)` on exactly three arbitrary dirty rows and a preserved source.

```text
cycle edges 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0: common price c > 0
insertion prices mu_i >= 8c; every reverse edge price >= 8c
exact complete tariff: min_i(mu_i) + 8c
```

The new lower bound is four cycle ADDs for the inserted source column. Arbitrary-dirty restoration requires four ADDs before the insertion as well, and a literal nine-gate word attains both bounds. The price cone excludes cheaper multiple-insertion or reverse-edge programs. At insertion/reverse prices 100 and cycle price 1, the exact optimum is 108. Discovery stopped at this first result.

The proof and verifier are in `research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff/`. Credit lee-phys for the triple, restoration contract and directed-price question; retain PR5259, Ali Romman Discussion5266/5300, Krzysztof Wojt PR5045, Ross Richardson PR3063/3121, Nick Petalas PR4916/5208 and the earlier fanout lineage. Their executables and numerical censuses are not replayed as this contribution.

## Evidence

- Before: destination-row tariffs leave the directed-cycle optimum unresolved. Three direct source insertions give a concrete bill of 300 at the displayed prices.
- After: a written arbitrary-word lower bound and an attaining dirty-restored word establish 108. The complete column graph has 343 states per root and target distance four; an independently arranged bit-coordinate search excludes every word through length three.
- A literal bit-list interpreter checks all 12,288 scalar input cases across the three roots, forward and inverse. Twelve rational price fixtures and 25 rejection controls pass. Each invocation prints a generated receipt bound to all five package hashes.
- Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized warning-strict direct checks pass, taking 0.108 and 0.104 seconds. Both registered commands pass; the complete launcher takes 0.419 seconds. These timings establish the replay budget, not a speedup.
- AST compilation, function-length inspection, whitespace checks, package metadata/pins and exact committed-byte/source-history checks pass at `ae5a8ec596517458b1ef3dc38fe8cb2aea6965a3`. The worktree is clean.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local absolute path. Standard library only. Expected statuses are `PASS_BOOLEAN_DIRECTED_CYCLE_TARIFF`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

This is a local tariff theorem for the declared ring, demand, three-row alphabet and price cone. It is not a finite search failure or a complete multiplication theorem. No arbitrary-price classification, extra-workspace theorem, physical native realization, complete supplier invoice, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Native/precision/tape/stock and full supplier replays were not run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Determine the exact tariff outside this cone with six independent ADD prices. The column graph handles the single-insertion branch; multiple insertions need a dirt-aware all-word lower bound. A physical application also needs actual complete gate prices and the full signed supplier bill.

## Related open work

- [PR6625](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6625) prices weighted pending-capacity query fanout; it has a different query/capacity contract and does not determine this Boolean edge tariff.
- [PR6577](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6577) studies a nine-target binary parity boundary with dirty workspace; its row-XOR target and alphabet differ from this three-row Boolean triple.

After CI, all 12 other open account PRs created since the advance CLAIM were inspected again. None studies this fixed Boolean triple with directed edge prices or computes its tariff. The existing adjacent fanout entries above remain applicable. Fresh complete overlap snapshots, main README searches, merged-work searches and live handoff claims found no competing result for this fixed tariff. Historical diffs and unpublished work are incompletely covered. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19377650).

## CI notes

Hosted CI passed at `ae5a8ec596517458b1ef3dc38fe8cb2aea6965a3` in [run 41669517107](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41669517107). The completed check list was read once: `plan` and `replay (research/boolean-directed-cycle-tariff)` both passed. The replay executes both registered normal and optimized scientific commands. Both commands and the committed-byte/source-history publication preflight also passed locally. No check was waived.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast Radius: isolated. Only one opt-in research package is added; existing source packages and the selected record are unchanged.
